note: The DECLARED record tier of every seed record, and the target mix for the 36 records Block F adds. Declared 2026-08-29 in F1, before a single new record was curated, for the reason ruling 39 gives about G3: a target set after the tranche exists is a target fitted to the tranche. F1_RULINGS.md rulings 43-45 carry the full argument; this file is the data.
declared_on: 2026-08-29, F1, at commit a6442b6, corpus 24 records, digest 26e4a683014bdf8a3dff98d48865a61869d137853333b82d024220c18eda9b28.
why_this_file_is_not_inside_the_records: Because a `tier` key on a seed record would MOVE THE CORPUS DIGEST. ingest.loader.canonical_record_text hashes the whole parsed record with sorted keys, so any new key changes that record's content_hash and therefore corpus_digest -- the denominator of all 396 Block E runs and of the sonnet arm's 165. F1 does not move the corpus (F1_START: 'F1 and F2 do not move the corpus'), and a tier declaration that silently invalidated every archived number would have been the most expensive tidy-up in this project's history. Checked before it was written, not after.
why_it_is_not_under_data/seed_corpus/: iter_seed_records REFUSES any .json under the corpus directory that is not at region/record.json depth -- glob('*/*.json') would not see a file at the top level and rglob('*.json') would, and a file some walks see and others do not is the exact failure that function exists to prevent. Only manifest.json is exempt, by name. So the sidecar lives one directory up, in data/, where no corpus walk reaches it. The layout guard did its job on the first file anyone tried to add since it was written.
why_declared_AND_derived: ingest.fidelity.derive_record_tier computes a tier from the record's chunks. If that were the only tier, it could never be wrong -- and could never be checked either. The declaration is what a curator believes the record is; the derivation is what the classifier reads it as; ingest.verify fails when they disagree. That is ruling 36's shape one level down: recorded and reconstructed are two kinds of knowledge and must be reported as two.

vocabulary.verbatim_with_provenance: Retrieval-eligible source-language text, a published translation, and BOTH CITED -- translation_source is non-empty. The SKZ / Periplus treatment.
vocabulary.verbatim_machine_english: Retrieval-eligible source-language text and NO ENGLISH TRANSLATION THE CURATOR COULD REACH, so resolve_english reaches the passage with `machine` or with nothing. RULING 57, F4, amends this from `no published translation`. The old wording claimed a fact about the world; derive_record_tier reads whether the record cites a translation_source, which is a fact about the record; and a curator can establish neither -- only that a search did not find one. FINDING 41 is the argument and this is the argument accepted rather than worked around: a definition satisfiable only by omniscience is satisfied in practice by whoever searched least. So the claim is about REACHABILITY, and every record in this tier carries in its notes the English-language search that failed -- the named sources consulted, any English found cited with its URL beside the reason it was refused as a translation_source, and the boundary where the search stopped. A record whose note says only that no English was found is not in this tier. Nothing checks this: whether a note names its sources is a judgement about prose, exactly as with why_gloss_capability_is_DECLARED, and a checker that counted source names would be satisfied by a list. AMENDED INTO THE VOCABULARY IN F1. PHASE2_PLAN's three tiers had no name for it, and F3-F7 predicts it becomes the common case: 'Local non-English sources mostly will not have published English, so resolve_english starts choosing machine and the Part 6 confidence machinery goes from dormant to load-bearing.' A mix cannot have a target for a tier that cannot be written down.
vocabulary.published_translation_only: No retrieval-eligible source-language text, and a cited published translation. No open original transcription available.
vocabulary.catalogue_record: source_type is a find, coin, object or artefact record. Both text fields are catalogue description whatever they contain, because classify_original forces object_description on these.
vocabulary.pointer_only: Nothing retrieval-eligible in either role: the record says where its text lives rather than carrying it. AMENDED INTO THE VOCABULARY IN F1, for arabia-02-palmyrene-tariff, which has been in this corpus since Part 3 and which none of the three original tiers held.
vocabulary.unclassifiable: NOT A TIER and refused as a declaration. What derive_record_tier returns when no tier holds a record -- ruling 36's shape, where an arm that cannot be identified blocks rather than being read as the default.

what_a_tier_is_deliberately_not: A fact about the aligner. answer.align.Pair.ground is section | index | document | none, and an unalignable published translation lands a reader on `published_document` rather than `published`. That is a real distinction, it is reported beside the tier, and it is never inside it: a tier that moved when align.py changed would stop being a property of the record, and the point of counting records is that the count means the same thing in F3 as in F7.

target_mix.why_these_numbers: PHASE2_PLAN names the failure directly -- 'so the tranche is not accidentally all catalogue records' -- and the reason it would happen is cost: a museum object record is the cheapest record in this corpus to curate and a cited bilingual inscription is the dearest. At 24 the split is 11 source-language-bearing against 11 catalogue. The target takes source-language-bearing records from 11 to 35 (46% to 58%) and catalogue from 11 to 19 (46% to 32%), because the product's central claim is about non-English source text and 22/30 is whether that text was reachable.
target_mix.pointer_only_ceiling: ZERO new pointer_only records. A record whose text lives somewhere else is a record the retrieval index cannot see, and the corpus already carries one as a standing F8 spike. Adding more would grow the record count without growing the corpus.
target_mix.why_per_region: Southeast Asia currently has ZERO records carrying retrieval-eligible source-language text, which is why all four of its gold cases sit on find records, and Africa, Persia and Scandinavia have one each. A tier target met entirely inside Arabia and South Asia would satisfy every aggregate above and leave four regions exactly as unable to answer a source-text question as they are now. Aggregate targets let a total failure in one region be paid for by successes in another, which is required_cases_note's argument about the floor, one level up.
target_mix.what_gloss_capable_MEANS_mechanically: The record carries, INSIDE A RETRIEVAL-ELIGIBLE CHUNK, both (a) a genuine alternative or hedged reading and (b) a statement that the reading is uncertain. Not in `notes` -- the notes field is not chunked and the model never sees it. This is not F1's invention: raqosh-epitaph's own note records that the case 'was nearly written' against the notes field, and oc-eo-medallion-legend's records that all three of the things it needs are retrieval-eligible. A hedge assertion the corpus cannot support is a case that can never pass.
target_mix.why_not_verbatim_machine_english: A refusable_with_gloss case requires the answer to quote a PUBLISHED hedged reading. On a record with no published translation the only English is machine, and quoting a machine translation of a disputed reading -- attached to a citation -- is the single worst output this system can produce, which is the thing the gloss arm exists to catch. A gloss case on that tier would be testing for the defect by requiring it.
target_mix.why_eight: The gloss arm is 3 cases against 22 answerable, and F1_START records that as a fact about the seed corpus rather than a defect: this corpus holds very few texts whose READING is genuinely in dispute. The sonnet arm then proved the assertions discriminate rather than being impossible -- vimose-runes went 0/12 to 5/5 with a real hedged gloss. So the arm is starved and its instruments work, which makes the supply of gloss-capable RECORDS the binding constraint, and the only moment it can be fixed is while the records are being chosen.
target_mix.what_the_six_COUNTS: Ruling 56, F4, 2026-08-31. Cases written against records that HOLD a reference_translation, and only those. On such a record both chunks are retrieval-eligible and in front of the model, so the assertion records WHICH one the quotation came out of -- which is the defect it was invented to see, measured at 45 of 45 across 16 archived runs of chinese-da-qin. On a verbatim_machine_english record there is no second chunk and the same words ask only whether anything resolved. ingest.fidelity.QUOTATION_CHOICE_TIERS holds the rule, because it is a rule and not a number. The six is NOT lowered: the number that belongs at 60 is not known from four, and lowering a bar because the cases behind it turned out to be weaker is a ruling of its own.
target_mix.why_the_vme_quotation_line_has_no_floor: Ruling 56 with ruling 53 in hand. A minimum on cases that can exist only on verbatim_machine_english records is a quota on a tier this block has just declined to decide the targetability of -- FINDING 41 -- so declaring one would re-target the residue through a different field. The teeth on this line are the PRESENCE check (a sub-tranche that omits the field is refused, because a zero it was given by default is a decision nobody made) and the capacity cap against its own vme slots. The number that belongs here is F5's to set, after ruling 53's deferred ruling, and it is owed.
target_mix.why: expect_quoted_from_original is true on exactly ONE case in thirty-three, weilue-chinese-quotation, which is also the corpus's only promotion candidate. One case is not a measurement of whether the answer path quotes source texts; it is a measurement of whether it quotes THAT source text. Six, one per region that will hold source-language records, is the smallest number that can tell the two apart.

allocation.declared_on: 2026-08-31, F3, before the first new record was curated. Ruling 51.
allocation.why_this_file_carries_it: Ruling 44 declared the mix at 60 and did not say which sub-tranche carries what, and F3-F7 curate roughly seven records at a time. An allocation decided at F7 is an allocation fitted to what was already curated: F7 would inherit every unmet constraint at once - four source-language records for Southeast Asia, eight gloss-capable records, six quoted-from-original cases - with no room left to fail and retry. Every aggregate tier target in this file is satisfiable inside Arabia and South Asia alone, which is why F1 declared the per-region floor and why the allocation has to name regions and not only counts.
allocation.the_ordering_principle: EVERY source-language record is curated before EVERY catalogue record, and the check refuses an allocation where that is not true. Hard regions go first: Southeast Asia has ZERO records carrying retrieval-eligible source-language text today, which is why all four of its gold cases sit on find records, and it needs four. If the block runs out of days, what is missing is catalogue records - the tier this corpus already has eleven of and the cheapest to curate - rather than the records the product's central claim depends on.
allocation.what_this_does_to_the_cost_column: It biases the AGGREGATE cost per record downward by construction, because the expensive tiers are curated first and the cheap tier last. That is not a defect to be corrected by re-ordering, it is the reason ruling 46 already reports per tier and in curation order: within a tier the ordering is untouched, and verbatim_with_provenance (14) and verbatim_machine_english (10) are the two tiers above min_n_to_read_as_a_trend and the two spread across four sub-tranches each. The aggregate is unreadable under this allocation and ruling 46 already forbids reading it. Said here so that nobody at G3 reads a falling total as efficiency.
allocation.gloss_and_quotation_are_CASE_quotas: gloss_capable is a count of RECORDS the sub-tranche must leave capable of carrying a refusable_with_gloss case; expect_quoted_from_original_cases and vme_quotation_cases are counts of gold CASES written in that sub-tranche. Seven quoted-from-original cases are allocated against a target of six - one per region that will hold source-language records - so that one may fail without the target failing with it. Ruling 56, F4: the two case fields are two questions and not one, expect_quoted_from_original_cases is capped by the sub-tranche's verbatim_with_provenance slots and vme_quotation_cases by its verbatim_machine_english slots, and both must be PRESENT. F3's numbers are its plan as declared and are not restated to match what it delivered; its vme_quotation_cases records the two cases that landed under a distinction that did not exist when its plan was written.

sub_tranches.name: F3
sub_tranches.why_these: The hardest eight in the tranche, first. Southeast Asia's four source-language records are the constraint no other region can pay for, and the four verbatim_machine_english records here are what turn on the machine-translation path: the verse and documentary confidence profiles are at n=1 and go load-bearing the moment the first one lands. Discovering that in F7 leaves no session to calibrate them in.

sub_tranches.name: F4
sub_tranches.why_these: Africa is at one source-language record of four and Ge'ez has no published translation for most of what is open, so it is the second-hardest region and the second-largest verbatim_machine_english draw.

sub_tranches.name: F5
sub_tranches.why_these: The last source-language records for the three regions that already clear the per-region floor, and the sub-tranche that completes the quoted-from-original quota at seven cases across seven regions.

sub_tranches.name: F6
sub_tranches.why_these: The last two source-language records sit here rather than in F7, so that the boundary between the expensive tiers and the cheap one falls inside a sub-tranche that still has a session after it.

sub_tranches.name: F7
sub_tranches.why_these: Catalogue records and published translations only - the tier that is cheapest to curate and the one whose absence would cost the corpus least, deliberately last.

target_mix.why_gloss_capability_is_DECLARED: Because it cannot be derived. what_gloss_capable_MEANS_mechanically defines it as a hedged reading AND a statement that the reading is uncertain, both inside a RETRIEVAL-ELIGIBLE chunk -- and only original_text_excerpt and reference_translation are chunked, which is the trap this list exists to make visible. Whether a passage hedges is a judgement about prose and no classifier here can read it, so the declaration is the claim and ingest.fidelity.check_delivery guards everything mechanical about it: that the record is one this tranche curated, that its tier can carry a gloss case at all, that the count does not exceed the quota, and that the quota is still REACHABLE from the slots the allocation has left. EMPTY AT F3 RECORD 26, and that is the finding this list was added for: two records were curated and neither carries its hedge in a chunked field, because the hedge was written into original_text_note, which the loader does not chunk.

how_curation_cost_is_reported: PER TIER, and against this mix. See ruling 45: G3's box 'curation cost per record recorded and trending down' is satisfiable by curating cheaper records, and the tier is the only thing that makes the number readable.
no_content_hash_is_stamped_here: Deliberate. An entry could record the record's content_hash at declaration time, so a record edited after its tier was declared would flag. It does not need to: the tier is DERIVED from the record on every verify run, so a record that moves into a different tier fails declared-vs-derived immediately, and a record that moves without changing tier has nothing to report. Stamping a hash would add a re-declaration to every corpus edit in F3-F7 and detect nothing the derivation does not.
